title: Embers sidemen: Clarence Johnson on piano, Joe Jones on drums
summary: The group was piano, bass and drums, usually with Clarence Johnson, whom he first met in Boston around 1926, and Joe Jones.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: In general, who did you usually have with you? Did you have piano, bass, and drums?
Piano, Bass and drums, yes. Uh-huh. Uh-huh. You mean personally?
Yeah, who was the -- with you -- usually, the piano -- pianist --

I'm trying to think now. First comes to my mind the very fine pianist, and the first time I met him, I met him in Boston, aw, 1926, '27, and he was quite a guy, and now he's -- with his arthritis and things, he's -- (snaps fingers) he can't play any more. Doggone, I haven't seen him in about two or three years, or -- Clarence Johnson.

Uh-huh, and what a musician! One of the -- what a man! Real fine guy. Well he was in there with me several times, on piano. Um, bass man. I can almost think of his nickname. I can't think of his first name.
Uh, not Shoobie-Doobie, and effective bass man, too. Very good big man. Well, I had to -- Joe Jones was in there also.
On drums. Several times he was --
